How does everyone else speed up their work? What are some tips for novice developers and designers?
How do you increase your output efficiency?

Pay attention to where you spend your time; in particular, pay attention to how you feel about spending your time on various tasks.

Whenever you're feeling like, "oh crap, this again", that's nature's way of telling you that you are doing something repetitive, brainless, and routine. That's a good sign that this portion of your work day can be automated, or better yet, designed away entirely.

Write as little code as possible. Try to solve every problem with a minimum of typing. Use existing libraries, or find sensible workarounds, or design around things when you can. Every line of code you write has to be tested and maintained and documented. It's just another straw added to the burden you carry.

Prototype. Paper is so much easier to change than code. If you are writing code for a user interface that has not been prototyped, you're going to do at least some of it twice.
